edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 for the Shares at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by the Seller.

3. Representations. The Seller represents that the financial statements provided to the Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company as of their respective dates and for the periods covered, in accordance with the accounting principles identified in those financial statements, consistently applied, subject, in the case of unaudited statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the terms of this Agreement confidential, except for disclosures to its professional advisers, financing sources and representatives who need to know such terms and are subject to confidentiality obligations, or disclosures required by applicable law or regulation. To the extent legally permitted, a party required to disclose shall give the other party prompt prior notice and reasonably cooperate in seeking confidential treatment. Neither party shall make a public announcement concerning the transaction without the other party’s prior written consent, except as required by applicable law or regulation.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price and Completion Accounts. For discussion and subject to Seller approval, the proposed enterprise value for the Shares is USD 40,000,000 on a cash-free, debt-free basis with a normalized level of working capital. The equity purchase price shall equal that enterprise value, plus only agreed qualifying cash, less agreed indebtedness and unpaid Seller transaction expenses, and plus or minus the difference between completion working capital and the agreed normalized working-capital target. Definitions, the target, illustrative calculations and accounting policies shall be agreed before signing. No item shall be counted more than once. The agreed accounting policies shall govern preparation of both the target and completion accounts, with an express hierarchy of policies and consistent treatment of items. At Closing, Buyer shall pay the estimated equity purchase price, less the agreed indemnity escrow, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to Seller’s designated account; the escrow shall be paid to the agreed independent escrow agent. Seller shall deliver an estimated closing statement at least five business days before Closing. Buyer shall deliver proposed completion accounts within 60 days after Closing, with supporting records and reasonable access for Seller. Seller shall have 30 days to object in reasonable detail; undisputed items shall be final. The parties shall seek to resolve objections for 20 days, after which unresolved accounting items shall be referred to an independent accountant jointly appointed by the parties, acting as expert and not arbitrator. Its determination shall be confined to disputed items and the parties’ submitted positions and shall be final absent manifest error or fraud. Expert costs shall be allocated by relative success. The resulting adjustment shall be paid within five business days after final determination. Non-accounting disputes remain subject to the agreed dispute-resolution provisions.

2. Signing, Closing and Conditions. Buyer’s satisfactory diligence shall be completed before signing definitive documentation and shall not constitute a further discretionary closing condition. The parties shall target Closing within 30 days after signing, subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the party entitled to the benefit of each waivable condition. Conditions shall include required regulatory and specified third-party approvals; absence of any legal prohibition; accuracy of fundamental warranties in all material respects and of other warranties except for inaccuracies that, taken together, would constitute a defined Material Adverse Effect, without duplicating embedded materiality qualifications; performance of material pre-Closing covenants; absence of a defined Material Adverse Effect; financing availability only on specifically agreed terms; and delivery of customary share-transfer documents, corporate approvals, payoff letters and releases of security. Material Adverse Effect shall be defined before signing with customary exclusions for general economic, market and industry developments, changes in law or accounting rules and announcement effects, subject to agreed disproportionate-impact exceptions. Any financing condition must identify the financing, require timely reasonable efforts to obtain it, restrict adverse changes to commitments and expire on an agreed date. Buyer shall not rely on a condition failure caused by its breach. The definitive agreement shall specify a calendar outside date, any limited regulatory extension and the allocation of approval and financing risk.

3. Warranties and Disclosure Schedules. Seller shall give negotiated warranties at signing and Closing concerning its authority and capacity; ownership of and title to the Shares, free of encumbrances other than agreed permitted encumbrances; Company organization and capitalization; financial statements and absence of undisclosed material liabilities; tax; material contracts; litigation; compliance with applicable laws; employment and employee benefits; and ownership or licensed use of material intellectual property. The scope, periods, materiality and knowledge qualifications shall be agreed before signing, with knowledge tied to identified persons and agreed inquiry obligations. Seller shall deliver disclosure schedules before signing, with cross-disclosure only where relevance is reasonably apparent on the face of the disclosure. Any data-room disclosure standard must be expressly agreed; general access to diligence materials shall not itself qualify all warranties. Seller represents that the financial statements provided to Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company as of their respective dates and for the periods covered, in accordance with the accounting principles identified in those statements, consistently applied, subject, for unaudited statements, to normal year-end adjustments and absence of footnotes. Those qualifications shall not excuse material misstatements or omissions or adjustments that would render the statements materially misleading. Buyer shall give customary authority, enforceability and no-conflict warranties and agreed financing representations. No warranty beyond those expressly stated in definitive documentation is given.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall protect the terms and existence of the proposed transaction and all nonpublic diligence and other information supplied by or on behalf of the other party or the Company, use that information solely to evaluate, finance and implement the transaction, and disclose it only to professional advisers, financing sources and representatives with a need to know who are bound by confidentiality obligations or professional duties. Each party shall be responsible for breaches by its permitted recipients as if its own, subject to expressly agreed exceptions for recipients independently bound directly to the disclosing party. Confidential information excludes information demonstrably public without breach, previously lawfully known, independently developed or lawfully received without restriction. Disclosures required by law, regulation or legal process are permitted; to the extent legally permitted, the receiving party shall give prompt prior notice, reasonably cooperate in seeking protective treatment and disclose only what is legally required. Neither party shall make a public announcement without the other’s prior written consent, except as legally required. On request following termination of discussions, information shall be returned or destroyed, subject to legal, regulatory and bona fide archival retention requirements and continuing confidentiality obligations. The definitive agreement shall preserve any existing confidentiality agreement except to the extent expressly superseded and shall specify the survival period.

5. Interim Operations and Access. Between signing and Closing, Seller shall procure that the Company operates in the ordinary course in all material respects and uses reasonable efforts to preserve its business. Subject to agreed thresholds, disclosed commitments, emergencies and legal requirements, Buyer consent shall be required for extraordinary distributions, issuances of securities, material acquisitions or disposals, new material indebtedness, material changes to compensation or material contracts, and material tax elections or settlements. Consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Buyer shall receive reasonable access on notice during business hours, without unreasonable disruption and subject to confidentiality, privilege, data-protection law and competition-law safeguards. Alternative arrangements shall be used where direct disclosure is restricted. Buyer shall not contact employees, customers or suppliers without Seller’s prior consent or exercise control over the Company before Closing.

6. Indemnification and Escrow. The definitive agreement shall provide indemnification for breaches of warranties and covenants and agreed pre-Closing tax liabilities, with reciprocal protection for Buyer breaches. General warranties are proposed to survive for 18 months after Closing; fundamental and tax warranties shall have separately agreed longer periods, and covenants shall survive for their specified performance periods and an agreed claim period. Timely notified claims shall survive until resolved. General warranty claims shall be subject to negotiated per-claim thresholds, a deductible basket and an aggregate cap. Separate limits for fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities shall be agreed. An agreed portion of the purchase price shall be held by an independent escrow agent to secure Seller’s covered obligations; the amount, duration, staged releases and treatment of pending claims remain to be negotiated. Releases shall retain only reasonably specified amounts for timely unresolved claims, with the balance released to Seller and retained amounts released promptly upon resolution. Claims procedures shall address notice, defense and settlement of third-party claims, mitigation, insurance and other recoveries, and prohibit double recovery, including for matters already reflected in price adjustments. Indemnification shall be the exclusive post-Closing monetary remedy for covered matters, subject to negotiated exceptions for fraud by the responsible party and express equitable remedies. All exclusions, caps and any fraud exception require definitive agreement.

7. Termination, Remedies and Status. Definitive documentation shall permit termination by mutual written agreement, for a final legal prohibition, for a material breach causing failure of a closing condition that is not cured within an agreed period after notice, and if Closing has not occurred by the agreed outside date. A party whose breach caused the relevant failure may not rely on that failure to terminate. Financing-related termination rights and any associated fee or other remedy must be expressly negotiated. Termination shall preserve accrued rights for pre-termination breaches and the provisions expressly stated to survive, including confidentiality and agreed dispute-resolution provisions. Specific performance and other equitable relief shall be available only on agreed terms, with financing-related limitations expressly addressed. Governing law, forum, service arrangements and any jury-trial waiver remain to be agreed. This draft is a nonbinding negotiating proposal, not an offer capable of acceptance, and does not bind either party to sell, purchase or negotiate; transaction obligations arise only upon execution of definitive documentation approved by both clients. Existing binding confidentiality obligations remain unaffected.

Fundamental warranties, taxes, identified diligence risks and fraud require separately negotiated treatment and survival periods. Although your cover note refers to revised interim covenants, indemnification and confidentiality, those operative provisions are not included. Please send the complete consolidated draft, including ordinary-course and anti-leakage protections, indemnity procedures and operative confidentiality language. Existing confidentiality obligations should remain unaffected.

All of the above remains nonbinding, subject to satisfactory diligence, Buyer approval and execution of mutually acceptable definitive documentation.
